trials.name: Footprint-pooled placement head
trials.hypothesis: Same conv body as the starting network. Each brick type's logit comes from max, min and mean pooling of learned features over that brick's exact footprint (anchored top-left), then a per-type linear layer. Max matches how landing height works and min matches 'every footprint cell fits the target', so sample efficiency should improve at almost no extra compute. Refuted if dev success is no better than the starting network's, within seed noise.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        c_in = spec.in_channels
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.fps = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.heads = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * WIDTH, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        outs = []
        for (dy, dx), head in zip(self.fps, self.heads):
            p = F.pad(f, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            mn = -F.max_pool2d(-p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            outs.append(head(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)).flatten(1))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.label: r1c2
trials.name: Residual body, global context, footprint head
trials.hypothesis: Three 3x3 conv layers at width 44 with residual connections, giving a 7x7 receptive field. Mean and max pooled context is broadcast back into the map before the last conv, and the footprint-pooled head is used. All of this stays under the starting network's FLOPs, so it keeps the full 16,384 steps. A wider view and global context should help with placement order (support before overhangs) and with avoiding cells it would seal off. Refuted if it does no better than candidate A or the starting network.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 44


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        c_in = spec.in_channels
        self.stem = nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.ctx = nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.fps = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.heads = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * WIDTH, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        h = F.relu(self.stem(obs))
        h = h + F.relu(self.conv1(h))
        g = F.relu(self.ctx(torch.cat([h.mean((2, 3)), h.amax((2, 3))], dim=1)))
        h = h + g[:, :, None, None]
        f = h + F.relu(self.conv2(h))
        outs = []
        for (dy, dx), head in zip(self.fps, self.heads):
            p = F.pad(f, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            mn = -F.max_pool2d(-p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            outs.append(head(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)).flatten(1))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1)
        z = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(z)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(z).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.label: r2c2
trials.name: Layer-aware 3D voxel net
trials.hypothesis: Each voxel gets its layer's build, target, missing and extra bits, plus the column heights, time used and a constant layer coordinate. These pass through a 3x3x3 conv, global context and a 1x3x3 residual conv at width 24 (about 1.06x compute). Pooling over the footprint gives a logit for each type at each layer, and logsumexp over layers gives the placement logit. This matches how a brick lands at one layer and has to match the target there. Refuted if it does not beat both round-1 networks.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 24


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = int(spec.Z)
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv3d(8, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.ctx = nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv3d(WIDTH, WIDTH, (1, 3, 3), padding=(0, 1, 1))
        self.fps = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.heads = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv3d(3 * WIDTH, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        Z = self.Z
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        build = obs[:, 0:Z]
        target = obs[:, Z:2 * Z]
        miss = obs[:, 2 * Z:3 * Z]
        extra = obs[:, 3 * Z:4 * Z]
        vox = torch.stack([build, target, miss, extra], dim=1)
        g2 = obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 3].unsqueeze(2).expand(B, 3, Z, Y, X)
        zc = torch.arange(Z, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype) / max(Z - 1, 1)
        zc = zc.view(1, 1, Z, 1, 1).expand(B, 1, Z, Y, X)
        x = torch.cat([vox, g2, zc], dim=1)
        h = F.relu(self.conv1(x))
        g = F.relu(self.ctx(torch.cat([h.mean((2, 3, 4)), h.amax((2, 3, 4))], dim=1)))
        h = h + g[:, :, None, None, None]
        f = h + F.relu(self.conv2(h))
        outs = []
        for (dy, dx), head in zip(self.fps, self.heads):
            p = F.pad(f, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool3d(p, (1, dy, dx), stride=1)
            mn = -F.max_pool3d(-p, (1, dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool3d(p, (1, dy, dx), stride=1)
            s = head(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1))
            s = torch.logsumexp(s, dim=2)
            outs.append(s.flatten(1))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1)
        z = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3, 4)), f.amax((2, 3, 4))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(z)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(z).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: There are no results yet, and scores are hidden, so these proposals rest on the task's structure rather than evidence. The budget is very small: 16 PPO updates. Any extra compute cuts training steps, so both candidates stay at or below the starting network's FLOPs and look for better inductive bias instead. The key per-action question is where a brick of footprint (dy,dx) lands, and whether the cells it fills match the target. Landing height is a max over the footprint's columns, and "all cells match" is a min over them. The starting network's 1x1 head has to learn this from a single cell's features. Candidate A keeps the starting body and swaps in a head that pools learned features over each brick's exact footprint (max, min and mean). Candidate B adds a residual body with a larger receptive field and global context fed back into the map, so it can judge placement order and overhangs. This lets round 2 separate the effect of the head from the effect of the body.
analyses.2: Scores are hidden, so the only evidence is that both round-1 designs trained without errors, at about the starting network's compute. Both use a footprint-pooled placement head. r1c2 also adds residual layers and global context. With one round left, the finalists will be the top two by dev score among four trials. That calls for one low-risk refinement of r1c2 and one new idea. The refinement adds dilation to the last conv so each cell's features cover nearly the whole 8x8 grid, at the same cost. The new idea uses the layer structure of the task. The 2D networks have to untangle per-layer channels to find where a brick lands and whether it matches the target there. A small 3D conv net keeps the layer as an axis. It scores each placement at each layer and combines them with logsumexp over layers. Compute stays near 1x.
